## Abstract

SLR Suite is an RStudio and Quarto workflow that links systematic-review protocols, executable analysis stages, validation evidence, and reporting. This software revision replaces a stateful launcher with isolated orchestration functions, adds explicit dependency and project metadata, introduces automated structural tests, and records reproducibility evidence in machine-readable artifacts. The bundled example supports verification of the workflow mechanics; it is not presented as evidence for substantive literature-review conclusions.

## Introduction

Systematic literature reviews require traceable decisions from search design through reporting. Earlier versions of SLR Suite combined scripts and documentation but did not provide a stable RStudio project contract, an explicit validation protocol, or a complete manuscript that described the executable architecture. This revision treats software, documentation, experimentation, and the paper as one research object.

## Software architecture

The system has six layers: orchestration (`R/`), numbered analysis stages (`scripts/`), protocol configuration (`config/`), evidence (`data/`), validation (`tests/` and `experiments/`), and reporting (`docs/`). Pipeline stages execute in isolated environments and append outcome records to a CSV log. Dependencies are declared before execution; the launcher does not mutate the user's global workspace or install packages at runtime.

### Module inventory

The nine ordered analysis modules are: M1 import and deduplication (`01_acquire_and_dedupe.R`); M2 protocol-driven screening (`02_screening.R`); M3 core bibliometric summaries (`03_biblio_analysis.R`); M4 VOSviewer network export (`04_vosviewer_export.R`); M5 theory–context–characteristics–methods matrix construction (`05_tccm_matrix.R`); M6 thematic evolution (`06_thematic_evolution.R`); M7 citation impact (`07_citation_impact.R`); M8 SPAR-oriented future-agenda aggregation (`08_future_agenda_SPAR.R`); and M9 PRISMA flow reporting (`09_prisma_flow.R`). Supporting modules define configuration dictionaries, VOSviewer thesaurus preparation, typed conditions, pipeline orchestration, quality gates, coverage measurement, and deterministic validation. The bidirectional mapping of modules, inputs, outputs, documentation sections, and tests is maintained in `docs/quality/software-documentation-traceability.md`.

### Installation and error handling

A user clones a tagged release, opens `slr-suite.Rproj`, installs `renv` once, and calls `renv::restore()` to reconstruct the package versions in `renv.lock`. No analysis stage installs packages. Missing dependencies raise a typed `slr_dependency_error`; missing paths and invalid arguments raise typed path or validation conditions; stage failures preserve the original parent condition and are recorded in the run log before the pipeline stops.

## Methods

The validation experiment checks repository invariants covering RStudio metadata, dependency metadata and lockfile, search and screening protocols, example input, ordered analysis stages, tests, technical documentation, software metadata, and quality evidence. It records the runtime platform, R version, timestamp, and individual pass/fail outcomes. GitHub Actions restores the locked environment on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows with R 4.5.1; parses all R sources; rejects runtime package installation and global-workspace clearing; runs unit and bundled-data end-to-end tests; enforces at least 70% core coverage; and uploads separate validation evidence for each operating system.

## Results

The repository supplies an RStudio project, a complete `renv.lock`, typed error conditions, reusable orchestration functions, regression and end-to-end tests, lint and coverage quality gates, a deterministic validation command, cross-platform CI automation, CodeMeta metadata, user and architecture documentation, quality evidence, and this technical paper. Local release validation passed 12 automated tests and measured 75.34% coverage of the core orchestration layer. Authoritative platform results are the status and artifacts of the CI matrix attached to the evaluated commit. Quantitative bibliometric results are intentionally not claimed until a frozen corpus, preregistered parameter set, and independently checked outputs are available.

## Limitations

Structural validation establishes that declared components are present and executable; it does not establish search completeness, screening reliability, coding validity, or correctness of domain interpretations. The included raw export is an example dataset and should not be generalized beyond workflow testing.

## Reproducibility and availability

Open `slr-suite.Rproj`, install `renv` once, run `renv::restore()`, execute `Rscript tests/testthat.R` and `Rscript test_all.R`, and then run `Rscript master_launcher.R validate`. Generated validation evidence is written under `artifacts/validation/`; CI publishes separate evidence bundles for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Source code, the traceability matrix, quality improvements, validation protocol, maintenance strategy, and version history are available from the project repository.

## Conclusion

The revision turns SLR Suite from a collection of scripts into a documented and testable research workflow. Its principal contribution is the explicit alignment of protocol, code execution, validation evidence, and manuscript claims.
